To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GLUT4-vesicles and PM contain VAMPs and syntaxins, respectively, that are in a SNARE complex that can be disrupted by NSF, alpha-SNAP and ATP, that the VAMPs are VAMPs 3 and 2, and that the syntaxins are syntaxins 4 and 2.
insulin treatment results in increased SNARE complex formation in PM of adipose cells.
insulin treatment of adipocytes increases the levels of GLUT4 in plasma membranes, and the efficiency of SNAP receptor (SNARE) complex formation with GLUT4 vesicles and plasma membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the SNAREs that mediate the fusion of GLUT4-enrichedd vesicles with the plasma membrane.
the molecular mechanism that regulates insulin action on GLUT4 translocation.
the identification of the SNAREs in adipose cells and with the formation of SNARE complexes in the presence of insulin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin stimulates GLUT4 translocation by increasing the formation of SNARE complexes between VAMPs and syntaxins 2, 3 and/or 4 in the PM and GLUT4 vesicles.
syntaxin 4 and VAMPs 3 and 2 are the major SNAREs in the PM of adipose cells, and that insulin treatment increases their interaction with GLUT4 vesicles.
the insulin-stimulated GLUT4 translocation pathway in adipocytes involves the formation of a SNARE complex between VAMP 2, syntaxin 4 and NSF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insulin-stimulated increase in GLUT4 vesicle fusion with PM is due to the formation of a SNARE complex containing VAMPs 1-3 and syntaxins 3-5.
the insulin-induced redistribution of GLUT4 from the LDM to the plasma membrane requires the assembly of a SNARE complex that includes syntaxin 4 as the t-SNARE and VAMPs 3 and 2 as the v-SNAREs.
insulin activates the fusion process by increasing the affinity of the VAMPs for the syntaxins in PM and by increasing the affinity between the VAMPs and NSF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VAMPs present in the GLUT4-enrich vesicles are VAMP2 and VAMP3.
the VAMPs present in GLUT4 vesicles are synaptobrevins 2 and/or 3 and that these VAMPs are in a form in which they can form SNARE complexes with syntaxin 4 in PM.
the SNARE complex that is formed between GLUT4 vesicles and the plasma membrane is the same in basal and insulin stimulated cells.
